cards.back: Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions — electron transfer metal → non-metal; giant lattice; high mp; conducts when molten/aqueous.
Shared electron pair between non-metals. Simple molecular (low mp, weak intermolecular forces) or giant network (diamond, SiO₂).
Lattice of cations in a sea of delocalized electrons — explains conductivity, malleability, high melting points.
Lone pair–lone pair > lone pair–bond pair > bond pair–bond pair. Lone pairs compress bond angles below the ideal.
2 domains linear 180° · 3 trigonal planar 120° · 4 tetrahedral 109.5° · +1 lone pair pyramidal ~107° · +2 lone pairs bent ~104.5°.
Unequal sharing from electronegativity difference → dipole. N–H, O–H and F–H bonds are strongly polar.
Polar bonds + asymmetric shape = polar molecule. Symmetric shapes (CO₂, CH₄, BF₃) cancel dipoles → non-polar despite polar bonds.
Present in ALL molecules; grow with electron count and surface area. Only force in non-polar molecules — explains I₂'s low boiling point vs diamond's hardness.
H covalently bonded to N/O/F attracted to a lone pair on another N/O/F. Strongest IMF — explains the boiling-point anomalies of H₂O, NH₃, HF.
Both giant covalent carbon. Graphite: 3-coordinated, delocalized electrons between layers → conducts + lubricates. Diamond: 4-coordinated network → hardest, insulates.
Ions are fixed in the lattice — charged but immobile. Molten or aqueous: ions free → conducts. Contrast metals (electrons always mobile).

cards.front: Why is I₂'s boiling point so low?
cards.back: Simple molecular: boiling overcomes weak London forces BETWEEN molecules — the strong I–I covalent bonds never break. Never say 'covalent bonds break'.

cards.front: Which molecules are non-polar despite polar bonds?
cards.back: CO₂ (linear), CH₄ (tetrahedral), BF₃ (trigonal planar) — symmetric shapes cancel the dipoles. CHCl₃ is polar (asymmetric).
Dative (coordinate) covalent: nitrogen supplies both electrons. Once formed, indistinguishable from the other three N–H bonds.

cards.front: O₃'s bond lengths — why equal and intermediate?
cards.back: Delocalized/resonance: the double bond character spreads over both positions → bond order 1.5, identical bonds. Same principle as benzene.
Single > double > triple bond LENGTH; triple strongest. C–C (ethane) > C=C (ethene) > C≡C (ethyne) in length — reversed for strength.
Four-step template: count domains → domain geometry → molecular shape (subtract lone pairs) → quote angle + polarity reasoning.
Identify structure (giant ionic / simple molecular / giant covalent / metallic) → name what's overcome on melting → compare strengths. 'Covalent bonds break' is WRONG for simple molecules.
Period 3+ elements can hold >8 electrons (SF₆ has 12 around S). Never for period 2 — C, N, O, F stop at the octet.
